title: A birational morphism is an isomorphism over a dense open, under quasi-compactness or finiteness hypotheses
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Schemes)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a birational morphism between schemes with finitely many irreducible components is an isomorphism over some dense open of the target, provided the morphism is quasi-compact or separated, and provided either it is locally of finite type with reduced target or it is locally of finite presentation. The proof first replaces the morphism by a finite one using the lemma that yields a dense open over which the morphism is finite, then separates the irreducible components of the target and reduces to an irreducible target, finds a nonempty open of the source mapping isomorphically onto the target as an open immersion, and finally removes the (closed, by finiteness) image of the complement of that open to obtain the required dense open over which the morphism is an isomorphism.
